next_steps: Jordan - send POC proposal & pricing sheet by 2026-09-13
Samir - share benchmark harness and run initial perf test with Avalon sample dataset by 2026-09-17
Priya/Ethan - provide 2 weeks of request traces and typical prompt sets by 2026-09-14
Schedule 60min pilot kick-off (benchmarks + infra access) for week of 2026-09-20
action_items: Jordan: Draft pilot agreement and reserved GPU options - due 2026-09-13
Samir: Prepare benchmark scripts (latency P95/P99, throughput) and quickstart doc - due 2026-09-17

summary: Discovery/POC scoping call focused on capacity sizing and autoscale strategy for AvalonAI's conversational AI POC. Discussed target latency and throughput, reserved GPU commit vs burst strategy, fallback policies (model variants, hosted fallback), telemetry needs, and security (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreed next steps: provide traces, run benchmark harness, and propose reserved capacity options.
topics: Benchmarks to run (P95/P99 latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens)
Fallback policies and compatibility (smaller quantized models, hosted fallback)
Security and network: VPC peering, KMS, SOC2
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intros, i'll kick it off — i'm jordan, AE for this region, and samir from our infra team will cover the nitty gritty.
[00:18] Maya (AvalonAI CTO): thanks jordan, maya here. we have ethan and priya on the line. high level: we want a two-week POC to validate latency and cost for our customer-facing assistant.
[00:30] Samir (Redwood SE): great, hey all. can you share current traffic shape? qps, typical prompt lengths, do you have bursts?
[00:42] Ethan: yeah so baseline is about 12 rps during business hours, peaks to ~80 rps for campaigns, average prompt ~180 tokens, 95th is ~420 tokens, that includes system+user.
[00:58] Priya: to add we expect peak campaigns twice a month that could push to 150 rps for ~10 minutes.
[01:10] Jordan: cool, so for POC we need to size reserved GPUs to cover baseline steady state and a burst strategy for those campaign spikes. do you have a hard p95 SLO?
[01:24] Maya: target p95 under 400ms for responses up to 256 tokens. business requirement. if we can't meet that, the app degrades.
[01:34] Samir: under 400ms p95 for 256 tokens is ambitious but doable with right model and GPU. quick question: is quality priority over cost, or do we want to optimize cost aggressively?
[01:46] Ethan: prefer quality for POC, we can tune cost later. but we still want a ballpark for cost per 1M tokens.
[01:54] Jordan: understood. our typical POC pattern: reserved capacity sized for steady baseline (e.g., 2-3 A100-equivalent GPUs depending on model), plus burst pool that can spin up additional instances for short peaks. fallback policies route to a smaller quantized variant or to hosted tier if necessary.
[02:14] Maya: can you explain the burst spin-up times? spikes are short so we don't want cold start penalties.
[02:23] Samir: sure. warm vs cold: cold start for new instance can be ~30-90s depending on image and model size. we mitigate with warm spare capacity and continuous tiniest-pre-warmed workers. for these 10-minute peaks we'd recommend a small warm buffer (one spare GPU) plus autoscale to add up to 2 more GPUs, and pre-warming the quantized variant for near-instant fallback.
[02:45] Ethan: what's the cost implication of keeping a warm buffer?
[02:49] Jordan: warm buffer is cheaper than failing SLAs — it's typically priced in the reserved capacity options. for POC we can propose an interim reserved commit for the baseline and allow burst billing for the extra GPUs. we'll provide cost estimates in the proposal.
[03:03] Priya: network/security: we'll need VPC peering or PrivateLink, KMS integration for key management, and SOC2 artifacts. do you support HSM?
[03:14] Samir: yes we support customer-managed KMS and HSM options on private deployments; hosted has KMS integrations. we have SOC2 and ISO docs, will share links. also we log per-request traces for audit.
[03:26] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:30] Maya: about benchmarks — what specific metrics will you run? we want reproducible numbers.
[03:36] Samir: we'll run latency benchmarks: P50/P95/P99 across prompt length buckets (<=64, 65-256, 257-512). throughput tests to determine max steady tokens/sec. memory and KV cache behavior under live sessions. cost per 1M tokens estimate with sample prompts. we'll also run quality checks against your evaluation prompts to ensure model fidelity.
[03:58] Ethan: can you use our sample dataset? we can't share full production but synthetic samples of top prompts are fine.
[04:04] Samir: absolutely — the more representative the traces the better. ideally we get 2 weeks of request traces with user/time distribution.
[04:12] Jordan: timeline suggestion: once we have traces and access, we'll run an initial benchmark within 3 business days and share results. POC total 2 weeks: week 1 sizing and baseline benchmarks, week 2 stress and burst tests + quality evals.
[04:27] Maya: that works. what are success criteria? beyond p95 we need correctness — NPS of internal reviewers?
[04:34] Jordan: recommend success criteria: 1) P95 latency <=400ms for <=256 tokens; 2) quality pass rate >=90% on curated eval prompts; 3) predictable cost estimate within +/-20% of forecast; 4) runbook for failover and autoscale policies validated.
[04:54] Ethan: ok good. on the autoscale policy, is scaling based on rps or token throughput?
[04:59] Samir: we support both. for model-bound workloads we recommend token throughput / GPU occupancy signals; for request-bound, rps with moving average windows. autoscaler uses a combination (primary token/sec, fallback to rps) to avoid oscillation.
[05:16] Priya: fallback policies — if burst capacity exhausted, what's recommended?
[05:20] Jordan: typical fallback: 1) route some traffic to a quantized smaller model (significant cost savings, slightly lower quality), 2) degrade non-critical features (e.g., reduce response length, remove embeddings-heavy steps), 3) as last resort route to hosted tier or queue requests with graceful retry. we can configure per-route policies.
[05:38] Maya: do you support canary/policy-based rollouts during POC? we might want 10% of traffic on new model and monitor quality.
[05:45] Samir: yes canary rollouts and gradual ramp with automatic rollback on quality regressions (we can hook into your eval set).
[05:52] Ethan: what metrics should we surface on the console for the POC?
[05:56] Jordan: minimal dashboard: per-route p50/p95/p99, token throughput, cost burn, queue lengths, and model quality alerts. Samir will set up alert runbooks for autoscale actions and fallback triggers.
[06:10] Samir: also, cache hit ratios (prefix/KV cache) are critical — good caching can reduce effective load by 30-50% depending on repetition.
[06:18] Maya: re caching — do you provide suggestions for which prompts to cache? we mostly have stateful chat sessions.
[06:23] Samir: we analyze prompt prefixes and suggest caching windows; session-aware caching for KV cache works well for chat. we'll include sample configs in the quickstart.
[06:32] Jordan: any objections on reserved GPU sizing now? based on the traffic numbers provided, initial recommendation: baseline reserved of 2x A100-equivalent for steady 12 rps with that prompt distribution, with burst up to +3 GPUs (warm buffer=1, autoscale adds 2), model variant: full FP16 for quality and 4-bit quantized for fallback.
[06:53] Ethan: sounds reasonable. can you map that to estimated cost per month? even rough numbers.
[06:58] Jordan: rough: reserved baseline (2 GPUs) monthly list price approximate $Xk (we'll send exact in sheet), burst billed at usage rates; for POC we can do a short-term reserved credit to reduce sticker shock. detailed numbers in proposal.
[07:12] Maya: about instrumentation — we need traces exported to our S3 and also to our Datadog. is that supported?
[07:18] Samir: yes we can stream logs to S3 and integrate with Datadog/Prometheus. we also provide link-level traces and token-level timing for latency breakdowns.
[07:28] Priya: what about data residency? some customers require EU-only processing.
[07:32] Jordan: we have regional routing; for POC you can pick a region. for production we support private deployments or VPC + regional constraints.
[07:41] Ethan: security review — we'll want SOC2, ISO, pentest reports before going to procurement.
[07:47] Jordan: we'll attach security pack in the follow-up (SOC2, ISO, pen test summaries, architecture diagram).
[07:54] Speaker 2: (mumbled)
[08:00] Maya: edge case question: if our peak is very short (under 2 minutes), would warm buffer be wasteful vs just queueing?
[08:08] Samir: depends on cost of user experience. queueing introduces delay; for user-facing chat it can be unacceptable. we can implement short-lived grace queues + progressive degradation: try smaller model first, then queue up to 30s, then fall back to shorter responses.
[08:26] Jordan: ok let's nail down what we need from Avalon to size properly: 1) 14 days of request traces (timestamps, prompt length, coarse client id), 2) top 20 prompt templates, 3) preferred region and compliance constraints.
[08:38] Ethan: i'll pull those — can redact user ids, keep time and length distribution.
[08:42] Priya: note we have strict egress rules; will share network diagram.
[08:46] Samir: perfect. on the benchmarking side we'll provide a harness (python scripts + docker) and an example runbook. link to harness will be shared: https://redwood.ai/poc-harness (placeholder).
[08:59] Maya: what's the typical length of a POC to satisfy procurement? sometimes procurement wants 30 days.
[09:04] Jordan: we do 14-day technical POC, then an optional extension if procurement or security needs longer; we can provide pilot discounts during procurement review.
[09:14] Ethan: about model variants — will you provide the exact model artifact names and sizes? we need to know memory footprints to ensure our infra will support them.
[09:21] Samir: yes, we'll include model pack manifest: model name, vram need, quantized size, expected tokens/sec per GPU.
[09:28] Maya: any known gotchas with KV cache warmups? we've seen cache thrashing on previous infra.
[09:33] Samir: cache shaping is important. for sessionized workloads, pin sessions to same worker to benefit KV cache; if you have high session churn, consider larger pool or shorter cache TTL. we'll run hotspot tests to estimate hit ratios.
[09:47] Priya: we want a clear rollback plan if performance or quality regresses during POC.
[09:51] Jordan: we'll provide runbook: immediate rollback route to previous model variant, automatic traffic cutover, and post-mortem template. also we'll enable canary thresholds for quality to auto-rollback at set fail rates.
[10:05] Maya: ok this is helpful. last thing — can you include a simple diagram showing how reserved + burst + fallback flow works? that's useful for procurement/security.
[10:12] Jordan: yes we'll include in the proposal doc and architecture diagram.
[10:16] Samir: for the POC acceptance we'll capture: 1) benchmark report, 2) quality evaluation report, 3) cost estimate, 4) runbook and network checklist — and those form the acceptance artifacts.
[10:29] Ethan: sounds good.
[10:32] Maya: anything else?
[10:34] Jordan: just to confirm next steps — samir shares harness, ethan/priya share traces, jordan sends proposal & security pack; schedule kickoff next week.
[10:42] Priya: will do.
[10:44] Jordan: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[10:46] Maya: thanks all.
[10:50] (call ends)
